zh.title: 航空公司一年通常招募多少空服員 美國每年約1.85萬個職缺
zh.summary: 美國航空公司平均每年產生約1.85萬個空服員職缺，大型航空公司每年招募1000至5000人，錄取率僅1%至4%；美國勞工統計局統計2025年空服員職位為13.37萬個，預計2025至2035年成長9%，波音預測至2045年全球需逾100萬名新空服員。
body: 美國航空業平均每年產生約1.85萬個空服員職缺，各航空公司的招募量視機隊規模、航線擴張與年度離職率而定。達美航空、美國航空、聯合航空與阿聯酋航空等大型航空公司每年例行招募1000至5000名新空服員，疫後復甦或機隊大量交付的高峰期可達8000人；中小型區域與低成本航空每年則招募數百至約1000人，流動率約4%至8%。大型航空公司常為數千個名額收到逾10萬份申請，招募多配合飛機交付與季節旅遊需求分批進行。

空服員錄取率極低：約90%的申請在第一階段即遭篩除，僅1%至4%的申請者通過，即使通過也未必完成訓練。多階段篩選包括篩選、面試、評量日、線上測驗、背景審查與體檢，常需3至6個月，其後還有6至8週的訓練課程。據Vertas Management資料，阿聯酋航空每月收到逾1.5萬份空服員申請；根據福斯新聞取得的達美航空招募紀錄，逾10萬名申請者中僅約1%獲聘，達美航空常為約1000至1200個職位收到逾10萬份申請。

以各公司規模來看，阿聯酋航空2024年1月宣布為迎接A350機隊招募5000名空服員，2023年已在353個城市聘用8000人，截至2023年8月空服員達2.15萬人，現估逾2.7萬人；美國航空現有空服員逾3萬人，達美航空與聯合航空各約2.8萬至3萬人，西南航空約2萬人；漢莎航空2025年招募逾2000人，瑞安航空空服員逾1.6萬人且仍在招募，澳洲航空計畫5年內招募600人。波音預測至2045年需102萬名空服員，每年約4萬個職缺，全球商用機隊預計每年成長2.4%；Aerviva預測至2045年需逾100萬名新空服員；歐盟與美國法規要求每50個乘客座位配置1名空服員，印度與南亞至2044年將需約5.1萬名新空服員。達美航空在亞特蘭大提供7週駐地訓練，聯合航空在休士頓提供6.5週訓練；全球每年空服員職缺估計約5萬個。

en.title: How many flight attendants do airlines typically hire in a year?
en.summary: US airlines generate around 18,500 flight attendant job openings a year on average, with major carriers hiring 1,000 to 5,000 new cabin crew annually and acceptance rates of just 1% to 4%. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 133,700 flight attendant jobs in 2025, projected to grow 9% from 2025 to 2035, while Boeing forecasts demand for over a million new cabin crew through 2045.
body: Across the aviation industry in the US, airlines generate around 18,500 flight attendant job openings per year on average. Each airline's hiring varies depending on fleet size, route expansion, and annual attrition rates. Major carriers such as Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, United Airlines, and Emirates routinely recruit between 1,000 and 5,000 new cabin crew members each year, rising to as many as 8,000 during major post-downturn surges or fleet deliveries. In contrast, smaller regional and low-cost airlines generally hire anywhere from a few hundred to around 1,000 cabin crew annually, covering base growth and typical turnover rates of around 4% to 8%. Major carriers often receive upwards of 100,000 applications for just a few thousand spots, so hiring occurs in competitive, periodic windows that match aircraft deliveries and seasonal travel demand.

Despite the growing need for flight attendants, acceptance rates are extremely low, with 90% of applications being filtered out at the very first stage. Only 1% to 4% of applicants make the grade, and even then, not everyone completes training. The multi-stage screening process can take months, including screening, interviews, assessment days, online assessments, security checks, and medical checks, and often takes between three and six months, followed by a six- to eight-week training course. Emirates reportedly receives over 15,000 cabin crew applications every month, according to Vertas Management. Just one percent of the more than 100,000 applicants get the job, according to Delta's hiring records obtained by FOX News, and major carriers like Delta frequently receive over 100,000 applications for roughly 1,000 to 1,200 roles.

In January 2024, Emirates announced it was recruiting 5,000 cabin crew for 2024 to coincide with the arrival of the new A350 fleet. In 2023, they hired 8,000 cabin crew in 353 cities worldwide, creating a large and diverse workforce of 21,500 cabin crew as of August 2023, and they are now estimated to have over 27,000 cabin crew. American Airlines now employs just over 30,000 flight attendants, ahead of rivals Delta and United, which each employ around 28,000 to 30,000 flight attendants, while Southwest Airlines has around 20,000. In 2025, Lufthansa recruited more than 2,000 flight attendants, Ryanair has over 16,000 flight attendants and is still recruiting, and Qantas plans to recruit 600 flight attendants within five years. Boeing has forecasted a demand for 1.02 million cabin crew members through to 2045, with around 40,000 openings every year, and the global commercial aircraft fleet is projected to grow 2.4% annually. According to Aerviva, forecasts predict the need for over 1 million new cabin crew members through 2045. Under EASA and FAA regulations, one flight attendant per 50 passenger seats is required for safety in commercial operations, and India and South Asia alone will need around 51,000 new cabin crew by 2044 as their fleets treble. Delta describes a seven-week onsite training program in Atlanta, United has a 6.5-week training program in Houston, and global cabin crew openings are estimated at roughly 50,000 per year.
